source.text: וַיַּקְהֵ֣ל דָּוִ֣יד אֶת־כָּל־שָׂרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל שָׂרֵ֣י הַשְּׁבָטִ֣ים וְשָׂרֵ֣י הַמַּחְלְק֣וֹת הַמְשָׁרְתִ֪ים אֶת־הַמֶּ֟לֶךְ וְשָׂרֵ֣י הָאֲלָפִ֣ים וְשָׂרֵ֣י הַמֵּא֡וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֣י כָל־רְכוּשׁ־וּמִקְנֶה֩׀לַמֶּ֨לֶךְ וּלְבָנָ֜יו עִם־הַסָּרִיסִ֧ים וְהַגִּבּוֹרִ֛ים וּֽלְכָל־גִּבּ֥וֹר חָ֖יִל אֶל־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And assembled David all [the] officials of Israel, [the] officials of the tribes and [the] officials of the divisions serving the king, and [the] officials of the thousands and [the] officials of the hundreds, and [the] officials of all [the] property and livestock of the king and of his sons, with the eunuchs and the mighty men and every mighty man of valor, to Jerusalem.

en.L: And David assembled all the princes of Israel, the princes of the tribes, and the commanders of the divisions who served the king, and the commanders of the thousands and the commanders of the hundreds, and the princes over all the property and livestock of the king and of his sons, together with the eunuchs and the mighty men and every mighty man of valor, to Jerusalem.
en.B: David gathered all the officials of Israel at Jerusalem: the officials of the tribes, the commanders of the divisions that served the king, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, and the officials who managed all the property and livestock that belonged to the king and his sons, along with the court officials, the warriors and every mighty warrior.
en.R: David called all the leaders of Israel to come to Jerusalem. They included the leaders of the tribes, the commanders of the army divisions that served the king, the commanders of units of a thousand and of a hundred men, and the leaders who looked after all the land and herds of the king and his sons. The palace officials, the famous fighters and all the other brave warriors came too.

decisions.choice: the leaders listed in chapter 27
decisions.reason: The groups named here are the ones listed in chapter 27: the commanders of the divisions that served the king month by month (27:1-15), the leaders of the tribes (27:16-22), and the officials over the king's property and herds (27:25-31). David had gathered the leaders of Israel once before, to set the Levites in order (23:2). Now he gathers them all to hand on the kingdom and the plan for the temple to Solomon.

decisions.choice: the eunuchs: high officers of the royal court
decisions.reason: The word can mean a eunuch, a man castrated to serve in a royal household, but it is also the usual word for a high court officer, whether or not he was a eunuch; Potiphar, who had a wife, is called by it (Genesis 39:1). Here it names officers of David's court.

decisions.choice: the mighty men and every mighty man of valor: David's famous warriors and the other men of proven strength
decisions.reason: "The mighty men" are David's band of famous warriors listed in 11:10-47. "Mighty man of valor" is a wider phrase for a capable, proven fighting man (7:2; 12:22), and can also describe a man of standing (Ruth 2:1). Together they take in every leading fighting man in the kingdom.

decisions.choice: princes / officials / leaders; commanders
decisions.reason: As in the terms used for these books: the word for a leader or official is "princes" at Literal, "officials" at Balanced and "leaders" at Readable; where it names the commanders of the army's divisions, thousands and hundreds, every level says "commanders".

decisions.choice: eunuchs / court officials / palace officials; mighty men / warriors / famous fighters; every mighty man of valor / every mighty warrior / all the other brave warriors
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "eunuchs", as the terms for these books do, with the sense explained in m2; Balanced and Readable say "court officials" and "palace officials". "Mighty man of valor" has the wording used throughout 1 Chronicles (7:2). Readable also says "units of a thousand and of a hundred men" and "land and herds" so that the list is easy to follow.

source.text: וַיָּ֨קָם דָּוִ֤יד הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ עַל־רַגְלָ֔יו וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שְׁמָע֖וּנִי אַחַ֣י וְעַמִּ֑י אֲנִ֣י עִם־לְבָבִ֡י לִבְנוֹת֩ בֵּ֨ית מְנוּחָ֜ה לַאֲר֣וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֗ה וְלַהֲדֹם֙ רַגְלֵ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ וַהֲכִינ֖וֹתִי לִבְנֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And rose David the king on his feet and said, Hear me, my brothers and my people: I [was] with my heart to build a house of rest for [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh and for [the] footstool of [the] feet of our God, and I prepared to build.

en.L: And David the king rose to his feet and said, "Hear me, my brothers and my people. I [had it] in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for the footstool of the feet of our God, and I made preparations to build.
en.B: King David stood up and said, "Hear me, my brothers and my people. I had set my heart on building a house where the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} could rest, the footstool of our God, and I made preparations for building it.
en.R: King David stood up and said, "Listen to me, my fellow Israelites, my people. I wanted to build a temple as a lasting home for the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The ark is like the footstool of our God, the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rests {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet as King. So I got everything ready to build it.

decisions.choice: I had it in my heart: I intended, I wanted
decisions.reason: "With my heart" means in his mind and will: it was what he meant to do. David first spoke of this plan to Nathan (17:1-2), and he told Solomon the same words (22:7).

decisions.choice: a house of rest: a settled, lasting place for the ark
decisions.reason: The ark had been carried from place to place since the wilderness (Numbers 10:33-36) and had stood in a tent in Jerusalem (16:1). A "house of rest" is a home where it would stay. The same picture is in Psalm 132:8, 14, "Arise, LORD, to your resting place", and the singers were appointed "after the ark came to rest" (6:16). The word also echoes the promise of rest to Solomon, "a man of rest" (22:9).

decisions.choice: the footstool of our God: the ark, with God pictured as a king enthroned above it
decisions.reason: The LORD is pictured as a king "enthroned on the cherubim" above the ark (13:6), with the ark as the stool for his feet (Psalm 99:5; 132:7). The "and" here joins two names for the same thing: the house is for the ark, which is God's footstool. God is not thought of as contained in the ark; it is the place on earth where the heavenly King meets his people.

decisions.choice: I made preparations: the gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood and stone David had gathered
decisions.reason: David had already stored up materials and workers for the temple (22:2-5, 14-16), and he will list his gifts again in 29:2-5.

decisions.choice: my fellow Israelites; the place where he rests his feet as King
decisions.reason: Readable says "fellow Israelites" for "brothers", since David is speaking to his people, not his own brothers. It explains the picture of the footstool in a short sentence (m3) and says "temple" for the house.

source.text: וְהָאֱלֹהִים֙ אָ֣מַר לִ֔י לֹא־תִבְנֶ֥ה בַ֖יִת לִשְׁמִ֑י כִּ֣י אִ֧ישׁ מִלְחָמ֛וֹת אַ֖תָּה וְדָמִ֥ים שָׁפָֽכְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And God said to me, Not you will build a house for my name, for a man of wars [are] you, and bloods you have shed.

en.L: But God said to me, 'You shall not build a house for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, for you [are] a man of wars and have shed blood.'
en.B: But God said to me, 'You will not build a house for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, for you are a man of war and you have poured out blood.'
en.R: But God told me, 'You will not be the one to build a temple for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, because you are a warrior and you have spilled blood.'

decisions.choice: a man of wars who has shed blood: as David told Solomon in 22:8
decisions.reason: David told Solomon the same thing in 22:8, in fuller words: "You have shed much blood and fought great wars." Neither place calls David's wars sins; they were the LORD's battles (14:10-16; 18:6, 13). But the house of the LORD was to be built by a man of peace, Solomon, whose name sounds like the word for peace (22:9). 1 Kings 5:17 gives another side of it: David was kept busy by wars all around him.

decisions.choice: a house for my name: the temple, the place where God makes himself known and is called on
decisions.reason: God's name stands for God himself as he makes himself known. A house "for his name" is the place he chooses to be worshiped and called on (Deuteronomy 12:5, 11; 2 Samuel 7:13; 1 Kings 8:29).

decisions.choice: blood: bloodshed, the killing of people
decisions.reason: The word "blood" is plural here, as often when it means blood shed by violence (Genesis 4:10). It points to the many killed in David's wars.

decisions.choice: a temple for my name; a warrior
decisions.reason: Readable says "temple" for the house, as in 22:8, whose wording this verse follows, and "warrior" for "man of wars".

source.text: וַיִּבְחַ֡ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵי֩ יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל בִּ֜י מִכֹּ֣ל בֵּית־אָבִ֗י לִהְי֨וֹת לְמֶ֤לֶךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְעוֹלָ֔ם כִּ֤י בִֽיהוּדָה֙ בָּחַ֣ר לְנָגִ֔יד וּבְבֵ֥ית יְהוּדָ֖ה בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑י וּבִבְנֵ֣י אָבִ֔י בִּ֣י רָצָ֔ה לְהַמְלִ֖יךְ עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And chose Yahweh [the] God of Israel in me from all [the] house of my father to be for king over Israel forever; for in Judah he chose for ruler, and in [the] house of Judah [the] house of my father, and among [the] sons of my father in me he took pleasure to make king over all Israel.

en.L: Yet {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel chose me out of all the house of my father to be king over Israel forever. For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose Judah as ruler, and in the house of Judah the house of my father, and among the sons of my father {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took pleasure in me, to make [me] king over all Israel.
en.B: Still, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, chose me from my whole family to be king over Israel forever. He chose Judah to lead, and among the people of Judah {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose my father's family, and from my father's sons it pleased {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to make me king over all Israel.
en.R: Even so, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, chose me out of my whole family to be king over Israel, and my family after me forever. He chose the tribe of Judah to lead. From Judah {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose my father's family. And from all my father's sons, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was glad to choose me and make me king over all Israel.

decisions.choice: the LORD's choosing: Judah, David's family, David, and then Solomon
decisions.reason: David traces a chain of the LORD's choices, each narrower than the last: the tribe of Judah, the family of Jesse, David himself, and in the next verse Solomon. The word "chose" comes four times in verses 4-6 and again in verse 10. The kingship is not something David won for himself; it is God's gift.

decisions.choice: ruler: the one appointed to lead
decisions.reason: The word means a leader set over others by God. Judah was to lead among the tribes (Genesis 49:8-10), and 5:2 says "Judah grew strong among his brothers, and a ruler came from him".

decisions.choice: among the sons of my father he took pleasure in me: David chosen over Jesse's older sons
decisions.reason: In 1 Samuel 16:1-13 Samuel passes over Jesse's seven older sons and anoints David, the youngest, because "the LORD looks on the heart". David's brothers are named in 2:13-15.

decisions.choice: king over Israel forever: through David's line of descendants
decisions.reason: David himself would die, so "forever" looks to the line of kings that would come from him, as the LORD promised in 17:11-14.

decisions.choice: my father's family; the people / tribe of Judah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "family" for the "house" of David's father and "people" or "tribe" for the "house" of Judah. Literal keeps "house".

decisions.choice: and my family after me forever
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the promise "forever" is for David's family after him (m4).

source.text: וּמִכָּ֨ל־בָּנַ֔י כִּ֚י רַבִּ֣ים בָּנִ֔ים נָ֥תַן לִ֖י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּבְחַר֙ בִּשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנִ֔י לָשֶׁ֗בֶת עַל־כִּסֵּ֛א מַלְכ֥וּת יְהוָ֖ה עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And from all my sons, for many sons has given to me Yahweh, and he chose Solomon my son to sit on [the] throne of [the] kingdom of Yahweh over Israel.

en.L: And of all my sons, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given me many sons, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has chosen Solomon my son to sit on the throne of the kingdom of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} over Israel.
en.B: And of all my sons, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given me many, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has chosen my son Solomon to sit on the throne of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s kingdom over Israel.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has given me many sons. But out of all of them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has chosen my son Solomon to sit on the throne and rule Israel for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because the kingdom belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the throne of the kingdom of the LORD: the kingdom is the LORD's, and the king rules it for him
decisions.reason: Chronicles says again and again that the kingdom over Israel belongs to the LORD and that David's son sits on the LORD's throne: "I will set him in my house and in my kingdom" (17:14); "Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king" (29:23; also 2 Chronicles 9:8; 13:8). The king of David's line is the LORD's deputy, not the owner of the kingdom.

decisions.choice: of all my sons he has chosen Solomon
decisions.reason: David's many sons are listed in 3:1-9 and 14:3-7, and Solomon was not the eldest. 1 Kings 1 tells how his older brother Adonijah tried to take the throne. Chronicles says only that the LORD chose Solomon, as he had promised (22:9-10).

decisions.choice: for the LORD has given me many sons: an aside within the sentence
decisions.reason: The words about many sons break into the sentence, which then picks up again with "and he has chosen". They stress how great a choice God made.

decisions.choice: rule Israel for the LORD, because the kingdom belongs to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable puts the aside first, as its own sentence, and spells out what "the throne of the kingdom of the LORD" means (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לִ֔י שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בִנְךָ֔ הֽוּא־יִבְנֶ֥ה בֵיתִ֖י וַחֲצֵרוֹתָ֑י כִּי־בָחַ֨רְתִּי ב֥וֹ לִי֙ לְבֵ֔ן וַאֲנִ֖י אֶֽהְיֶה־לּ֥וֹ לְאָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to me, Solomon your son, he will build my house and my courts, for I have chosen him for me for a son, and I will be to him for a father.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, 'Solomon your son, he will build {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} courts, for I have chosen him to be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} son, and I will be to him a father.
en.B: He said to me, 'Your son Solomon is the one who will build {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} courts. I have chosen him as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} son, and I will be a father to him.
en.R: He told me, 'Your son Solomon is the one who will build {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} temple and its courtyards. I have chosen him as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} son, and I will be his father.

decisions.choice: he will build my house; I will be his father: the promise of 17:12-13 and 22:10
decisions.reason: The words repeat the LORD's promise through Nathan (17:12-13) and David's words to Solomon (22:10). What is new is "I have chosen him": in 17:11 the son who would build was not named. Now God's choice is said to fall on Solomon.

decisions.choice: my son, his father: a bond of covenant care and loyalty
decisions.reason: As in 17:13: the LORD takes the king into a relation like that of father and son. He will care for him and guide him, and the king is to honor and obey him (Psalm 2:7; 89:27-28).

decisions.choice: he will build: he, and no one else
decisions.reason: The word "he" is stressed, as in 17:12: it is Solomon, not David, who will build.

decisions.choice: my courts: the open courtyards around the temple
decisions.reason: The temple stood within walled courtyards where the people gathered and the altar stood (verse 12; 1 Kings 6:36; 2 Chronicles 4:9).

decisions.choice: I will be to him a father (Literal); I will be a father to him (Balanced); I will be his father (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level uses the same wording as 17:13.

source.text: וַהֲכִינוֹתִ֥י אֶת־מַלְכוּת֖וֹ עַד־לְעוֹלָ֑ם אִם־יֶחֱזַ֗ק לַעֲשׂ֛וֹת מִצְוֺתַ֥י וּמִשְׁפָּטַ֖י כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will establish his kingdom until forever, if he will be strong to do my commandments and my judgments as the day the this.

en.L: And I will establish his kingdom forever, if he is resolute to do {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments, as [at] this day.'
en.B: I will make his kingdom firm forever if he holds firmly to doing {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings, as he does today.'
en.R: I will make his kingdom last forever, if he keeps on obeying {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands and rules as he does now.'

decisions.choice: if he is resolute: the promise to Solomon himself depends on his obedience
decisions.reason: The promise to David's line was given without condition (17:13-14). Here a condition is added for Solomon: his kingdom will stand if he keeps on obeying. David says the same to Solomon in verse 9, and the LORD says it to him in 2 Chronicles 7:17-22 (1 Kings 9:4-9).

decisions.choice: be resolute: be strong, hold firm
decisions.reason: The verb means to be strong. Here it is to hold on firmly and keep on doing what God commands. It is the same verb as "be strong" in verses 10 and 20.

decisions.choice: as at this day: as he does now
decisions.reason: The phrase means "as is the case today". It most likely says that Solomon is to go on obeying as he does at present. It could also mean "as you see today", pointing to the present moment as proof, but the sense of the condition is the same.

decisions.choice: commandments and judgments / commandments and rulings / commands and rules
decisions.reason: As in the terms used for these books, from Numbers to Ruth.

source.text: וְ֠עַתָּה לְעֵינֵ֨י כָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל קְהַל־יְהוָה֙ וּבְאָזְנֵ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ שִׁמְר֣וּ וְדִרְשׁ֔וּ כָּל־מִצְוֺ֖ת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם לְמַ֤עַן תִּֽירְשׁוּ֙ אֶת־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה וְהִנְחַלְתֶּ֛ם לִבְנֵיכֶ֥ם אַחֲרֵיכֶ֖ם עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And now, to [the] eyes of all Israel, [the] assembly of Yahweh, and in [the] ears of our God: keep and seek all [the] commandments of Yahweh your God, so that you may possess the land the good and cause [it] to inherit to your sons after you until forever.

en.L: And now, in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and in the hearing of our God: keep and seek all the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, so that you may possess the good land and leave [it] as an inheritance to your {{gender:children|sons}} after you forever.
en.B: So now, before the eyes of all Israel, the assembly of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and with our God listening, I charge you: keep all the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and seek them out, so that you may keep possession of the good land and leave it to your descendants after you as their inheritance forever.
en.R: So now, with all Israel here as witnesses, the people gathered for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and with our God listening, I tell you this: Be careful to obey all the commands of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and try hard to know them. Then you will keep this good land and pass it on to your descendants to be theirs forever.

decisions.choice: in the sight of all Israel and in the hearing of our God: a solemn charge before witnesses
decisions.reason: David gives his charge in front of the whole gathering and with God himself as a hearer. Both are witnesses to what is asked of the people and of Solomon.

decisions.choice: keep, seek, your God: spoken to the whole assembly
decisions.reason: The verbs and the word "your" are plural here: David speaks to all who are gathered. In verse 9 he turns to Solomon alone.

decisions.choice: seek: search out, give careful attention to
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek or inquire. With commandments it means to study them and care about doing them. The same verb comes twice in verse 9: the LORD "searches" all hearts, and "if you seek him".

decisions.choice: possess the good land and leave it as an inheritance: keep hold of the land and pass it on
decisions.reason: Israel already lived in the land. The words echo Moses' promises (Deuteronomy 4:1, 21-22, 40; 6:18): obedience keeps the people in the land and lets them hand it down to their children. Disobedience would lose it (Deuteronomy 4:25-27).

decisions.choice: I charge you / I tell you this
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add these words so that the long opening phrase leads clearly into the commands.

decisions.choice: your children / your sons
decisions.reason: The word "sons" here means descendants, men and women. Literal gives "children" with "sons" as the alternative; Balanced and Readable say "descendants".

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה שְׁלֹמֹֽה־בְנִ֡י דַּע֩ אֶת־אֱלֹהֵ֨י אָבִ֜יךָ וְעָבְדֵ֗הוּ בְּלֵ֤ב שָׁלֵם֙ וּבְנֶ֣פֶשׁ חֲפֵצָ֔ה כִּ֤י כָל־לְבָבוֹת֙ דּוֹרֵ֣שׁ יְהוָ֔ה וְכָל־יֵ֥צֶר מַחֲשָׁב֖וֹת מֵבִ֑ין אִֽם־תִּדְרְשֶׁ֨נּוּ֙ יִמָּ֣צֵא לָ֔ךְ וְאִם־תַּֽעַזְבֶ֖נּוּ יַזְנִיחֲךָ֥ לָעַֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, Solomon my son, know [the] God of your father and serve him with a heart complete and with a soul willing, for all hearts [is] searching Yahweh, and every inclination of thoughts [he is] understanding. If you seek him, he will be found by you, and if you forsake him, he will reject you to forever.

en.L: And you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with a complete heart and with a willing soul, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} searches all hearts and understands every intention of the thoughts. If you seek {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be found by you; but if you forsake {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will reject you forever.
en.B: As for you, my son Solomon, know your father's God, and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with an undivided heart and a willing soul, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} searches every heart and understands every intention behind people's thoughts. If you seek {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will let you find {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; but if you abandon {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will reject you forever.
en.R: And you, Solomon my son, come to know the God your father serves. Serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all your heart, gladly and willingly. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} looks into every heart, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} understands every plan and every thought. If you look for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, you will find {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But if you turn away from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will reject you forever.

decisions.choice: know the God of your father: know him personally and be loyal to him
decisions.reason: To "know" God is more than to know about him: it is to recognize him as one's own God, trust him and do what he wants (Jeremiah 22:16; Hosea 6:6). "The God of your father" is the God David has known and served (Genesis 26:24; 31:5).

decisions.choice: a complete heart and a willing soul: undivided loyalty given gladly
decisions.reason: A "complete" heart is whole and undivided, loyal without holding back, as in 12:39 and 29:9, 19. A "willing soul" serves with desire and delight, not by force. The two phrases together ask for the whole person.

decisions.choice: every intention of the thoughts: what people plan and purpose inside
decisions.reason: The first word means something formed or shaped, and so the purpose a person forms in the mind; Genesis 6:5 and 8:21 use it of the inclinations of the human heart. David prays in 29:18 that the LORD will keep such purposes in his people's hearts.

decisions.choice: if you seek him he will be found by you; if you forsake him he will reject you
decisions.reason: God lets himself be found by those who seek him, and he casts off those who leave him. The prophet Azariah says the same to King Asa (2 Chronicles 15:2), and Moses and Jeremiah promise it (Deuteronomy 4:29; Jeremiah 29:13-14). Solomon later turned from the LORD in his old age (1 Kings 11:4-11), though Chronicles does not tell that part of his story.

decisions.choice: a complete heart / an undivided heart / with all your heart
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced use the same words as 12:39. Readable says "with all your heart, gladly and willingly" to explain both phrases (m2), and "look into" for "search".

decisions.choice: he will let you find him / you will find him
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he will be found by you": God lets himself be found. Balanced keeps God as the one who acts; Readable says it from the seeker's side, which is the same in meaning.

source.text: רְאֵ֣ה׀עַתָּ֗ה כִּֽי־יְהוָ֛ה בָּ֧חַר בְּךָ֛ לִבְנֽוֹת־בַּ֥יִת לַמִּקְדָּ֖שׁ חֲזַ֥ק וַעֲשֵֽׂה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: See now, for Yahweh has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary; be strong and act.

en.L: See now, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong and act."
en.B: Consider this now: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has chosen you to build a house to be the sanctuary. Be strong and do the work."
en.R: Think about it: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has chosen you to build a temple to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy place. Be strong and get to work."

decisions.choice: the sanctuary: the holy place where God dwells among his people
decisions.reason: The word means a holy place. It is used of the tabernacle, which God told Moses to make so that he could live among his people (Exodus 25:8).

decisions.choice: be strong and act: take courage and carry out the task
decisions.reason: The two commands together urge someone to stop holding back and get on with a task (Ezra 10:4). David will say it again, more fully, in verse 20.

decisions.choice: the LORD has chosen you
decisions.reason: This is the last link in the chain of the LORD's choices (verses 4-6). Solomon builds because God has chosen him to.

decisions.choice: act / do the work / get to work
decisions.reason: The verb "do" has no object. Literal keeps the bare "act"; Balanced and Readable say what is to be done, the work of building.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן דָּוִ֣יד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֡וֹ אֶת־תַּבְנִ֣ית הָאוּלָם֩ וְֽאֶת־בָּ֨תָּ֜יו וְגַנְזַכָּ֧יו וַעֲלִיֹּתָ֛יו וַחֲדָרָ֥יו הַפְּנִימִ֖ים וּבֵ֥ית הַכַּפֹּֽרֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And gave David to Solomon his son [the] pattern of the porch and its houses and its treasuries and its upper rooms and its rooms the inner and [the] house of the mercy seat,

en.L: And David gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch and of its houses and its treasuries and its upper rooms and its inner rooms and the house of the mercy seat,
en.B: Then David gave his son Solomon the plans for the porch of the temple, its buildings, its treasuries, its upper rooms, its inner rooms and the room for the mercy seat,
en.R: Then David gave his son Solomon the plans for the temple. They showed the porch at the front, the buildings, the storerooms for treasure, the upstairs rooms, the inner rooms, and the room for the gold lid of the ark, the place where sins are covered.

decisions.choice: pattern: the design of the temple, as Moses received the design of the tabernacle
decisions.reason: The word means a form, design or model. It is the word for the pattern of the tabernacle that God showed Moses on the mountain (Exodus 25:9, 40). As Moses was given the design of the tabernacle, David now hands on the design of the temple, and verse 19 says it came from the LORD. The word comes four times in verses 11-19.

decisions.choice: the porch and its houses: the entrance hall and the parts of the temple building
decisions.reason: The porch was the entrance hall at the front of the temple (1 Kings 6:3). "Its houses" are the parts of the building behind it: the main hall, the inner room and the rooms built against the walls (1 Kings 6:5).

decisions.choice: its treasuries: storerooms for valuables
decisions.reason: This word for a treasury is found only here in the Old Testament; it is a word borrowed from Persian. Verse 12 uses the usual Hebrew word for the same rooms.

decisions.choice: the house of the mercy seat: the most holy place
decisions.reason: The innermost room of the temple, where the ark stood, is named here after the gold lid of the ark, the mercy seat (Exodus 25:17-22). There the high priest made atonement once a year (Leviticus 16:2, 14-16).

decisions.choice: plans; buildings
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "pattern", the same word as in Exodus 25:9, 40. Balanced and Readable say "plans", since what David hands over is the design of a whole set of buildings. They say "buildings" for "houses" and "room" for "the house of" the mercy seat.

decisions.choice: the gold lid of the ark, the place where sins are covered
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 25:17, Readable explains the mercy seat instead of using the name.

source.text: וְתַבְנִ֗ית כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה בָר֨וּחַ֙ עִמּ֔וֹ לְחַצְר֧וֹת בֵּית־יְהוָ֛ה וּלְכָל־הַלְּשָׁכ֖וֹת סָבִ֑יב לְאֹֽצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וּלְאֹצְר֖וֹת הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים׃

records.literal_gloss: and [the] pattern of all that was in the spirit with him, for [the] courts of [the] house of Yahweh and for all the chambers around, for [the] treasuries of [the] house of God and for [the] treasuries of the holy things,

en.L: and the pattern of all that was in the spirit with him, for the courts of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for all the chambers all around, for the treasuries of the house of God and for the treasuries of the holy things,
en.B: and the plans for everything he had in mind: the courts of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house and all the rooms around them, the treasuries of God's house and the treasuries for the dedicated gifts,
en.R: He gave him the plans for everything he had in mind: the courtyards of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple and all the rooms around them, and the storerooms for the treasures of God's temple and for the gifts given to God.

decisions.choice: all that was in the spirit with him: all that he had in mind
alternatives: all that he had by the Spirit
decisions.reason: The word can mean a person's spirit or mind, and "what comes into your spirit" is what someone thinks or plans (Ezekiel 11:5; 20:32). So the plan is what David had in mind. But the word is also used of the Spirit of God, and the phrase could mean "all that he had by the Spirit"; verse 19 does say the plan came from the LORD. The wording here does not settle which is meant.

decisions.choice: the chambers all around: rooms built around the courts
decisions.reason: Rooms were built around the temple courts for the priests and Levites and for storing supplies (9:26, 33; 23:28; Jeremiah 35:4).

decisions.choice: the holy things: gifts dedicated to the LORD
decisions.reason: These are things made holy by being given to the LORD, such as the silver and gold David took in his wars and dedicated (18:11). Levites were put in charge of their treasuries (26:20, 26-28).

decisions.choice: all that he had in mind
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the more likely sense (m1); Literal keeps "in the spirit with him", which leaves room for the other.

source.text: וּֽלְמַחְלְקוֹת֙ הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם וּֽלְכָל־מְלֶ֖אכֶת עֲבוֹדַ֣ת בֵּית־יְהוָ֑ה וּֽלְכָל־כְּלֵ֖י עֲבוֹדַ֥ת בֵּית־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and for [the] divisions of the priests and the Levites, and for all [the] work of [the] service of [the] house of Yahweh, and for all [the] articles of [the] service of [the] house of Yahweh,

en.L: and for the divisions of the priests and the Levites, and for all the work of the service of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and for all the articles of the service of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.B: for the priests' and Levites' divisions, for all the work of serving in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house, and for all the articles used in the service of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house,
en.R: He also gave him the plans for the groups of priests and Levites who would take turns serving, for all the work to be done in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple, and for all the things used in the worship there.

decisions.choice: the divisions of the priests and the Levites: the groups set out in chapters 23-26
decisions.reason: David had divided the priests into twenty-four divisions that took turns serving (24:1-19), and had set the Levites in groups for their duties (23:6-32; chapters 25-26). These arrangements are part of what he hands on to Solomon.

decisions.choice: the service: the work of worship in the temple
decisions.reason: The word means work or service, and here the duties of worship: the sacrifices, the singing, the guarding of the gates and the care of the holy things (23:28-32).

decisions.choice: the list goes on: all this was part of the plan David gave
decisions.reason: Each item begins "for", as in verse 12. They all depend on "David gave ... the pattern" in verse 11, and the list runs to the end of verse 18.

decisions.choice: who would take turns serving
decisions.reason: Readable says what the divisions were for (m1).

source.text: לַזָּהָ֤ב בַּמִּשְׁקָל֙ לַזָּהָ֔ב לְכָל־כְּלֵ֖י עֲבוֹדָ֣ה וַעֲבוֹדָ֑ה לְכֹ֨ל כְּלֵ֤י הַכֶּ֨סֶף֙ בְּמִשְׁקָ֔ל לְכָל־כְּלֵ֖י עֲבוֹדָ֥ה וַעֲבוֹדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: for the gold by weight for gold, for all articles of service and service; for all articles of the silver by weight, for all articles of service and service,

en.L: for the gold by weight, for [articles of] gold, for all the articles of each service; for all the articles of silver by weight, for all the articles of each service,
en.B: the weight of gold for all the gold articles used in each kind of service, and the weight of silver for all the silver articles used in each kind of service,
en.R: He told him how much gold to use for each gold object used in worship, and how much silver for each silver object.

decisions.choice: service and service: each kind of service
decisions.reason: Saying a word twice is a Hebrew way of saying "each" or "every". The same pattern comes in verses 15-17: "lampstand and lampstand", "table and table", "bowl and bowl".

decisions.choice: for the gold by weight: David set the weight of metal for each object
decisions.reason: The list in verses 14-18 names the gold and silver David set aside, weighed out for each object. David had already gathered great amounts of both (22:14; 29:2-4).

decisions.choice: each gold object used in worship
decisions.reason: Readable puts the long list in a plain sentence, and says "used in worship" for "of service".

source.text: וּמִשְׁקָ֞ל לִמְנֹר֣וֹת הַזָּהָ֗ב וְנֵרֹֽתֵיהֶם֙ זָהָ֔ב בְּמִשְׁקַל־מְנוֹרָ֥ה וּמְנוֹרָ֖ה וְנֵרֹתֶ֑יהָ וְלִמְנֹר֨וֹת הַכֶּ֤סֶף בְּמִשְׁקָל֙ לִמְנוֹרָ֣ה וְנֵרֹתֶ֔יהָ כַּעֲבוֹדַ֖ת מְנוֹרָ֥ה וּמְנוֹרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and [the] weight for [the] lampstands of the gold and their lamps of gold, by [the] weight of lampstand and lampstand and its lamps; and for [the] lampstands of the silver by weight for lampstand and its lamps, according to [the] service of lampstand and lampstand,

en.L: and the weight for the lampstands of gold and their lamps of gold, by the weight of each lampstand and its lamps; and for the lampstands of silver by weight, for a lampstand and its lamps, according to the use of each lampstand,
en.B: the weight of the gold lampstands and their gold lamps, with the weight for each lampstand and its lamps; and the weight of the silver lampstands, for each lampstand and its lamps, according to the use of each lampstand,
en.R: He told him how much gold to use for each gold lampstand and its lamps, and how much silver for each silver lampstand and its lamps, depending on how each one would be used.

decisions.choice: the gold lampstands: there were ten in Solomon's temple
decisions.reason: The tabernacle had one gold lampstand with seven lamps (Exodus 25:31-40). Solomon's temple had ten, five on each side in front of the inner room (1 Kings 7:49; 2 Chronicles 4:7).

decisions.choice: the silver lampstands: not mentioned anywhere else
decisions.reason: Silver lampstands are not described anywhere else in the Old Testament. Their use "according to the use of each" is not explained; they may have lit the side rooms or other parts of the temple.

decisions.choice: lampstand and lampstand: each lampstand
decisions.reason: As in verse 14, the doubled word means "each".

decisions.choice: depending on how each one would be used
decisions.reason: Readable says "use" for the word "service" here, as Literal and Balanced do, since it is the purpose of each lampstand.

source.text: וְאֶת־הַזָּהָ֥ב מִשְׁקָ֛ל לְשֻׁלְחֲנ֥וֹת הַֽמַּעֲרֶ֖כֶת לְשֻׁלְחַ֣ן וְשֻׁלְחָ֑ן וְכֶ֖סֶף לְשֻׁלְחֲנ֥וֹת הַכָּֽסֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: and the gold [by] weight for [the] tables of the row, for table and table, and silver for [the] tables of the silver,

en.L: and the gold by weight for the tables of the rows [of bread], for each table, and silver for the tables of silver,
en.B: the weight of gold for each of the tables for the rows of holy bread, and silver for the silver tables,
en.R: He told him how much gold to use for each table where the holy bread was set out in rows, and how much silver for the silver tables.

decisions.choice: the tables of the rows: the tables for the bread of the Presence
decisions.reason: "The row" is the bread set out in two rows on the table before the LORD every Sabbath (Leviticus 24:5-8), elsewhere called the bread of the Presence (Exodus 25:30). The Levites prepared it (9:32; 23:29). The word is plural here: 2 Chronicles 4:8, 19 tells of ten tables, while 1 Kings 7:48 names one.

decisions.choice: the silver tables: not mentioned anywhere else
decisions.reason: Like the silver lampstands, the silver tables are not described anywhere else, and their use is not known.

decisions.choice: [of bread] / of holy bread / the holy bread
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "the row". Literal adds "of bread" in brackets; Balanced and Readable name the holy bread (m1).

source.text: וְהַמִּזְלָג֧וֹת וְהַמִּזְרָק֛וֹת וְהַקְּשָׂוֺ֖ת זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר וְלִכְפוֹרֵ֨י הַזָּהָ֤ב בְּמִשְׁקָל֙ לִכְפ֣וֹר וּכְפ֔וֹר וְלִכְפוֹרֵ֥י הַכֶּ֛סֶף בְּמִשְׁקָ֖ל לִכְפ֥וֹר וּכְפֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: and the forks and the basins and the jugs, gold pure; and for [the] bowls of the gold by weight for bowl and bowl, and for [the] bowls of the silver by weight for bowl and bowl,

en.L: and the forks and the basins and the pitchers, [of] pure gold; and for the bowls of gold, by weight for each bowl; and for the bowls of silver, by weight for each bowl,
en.B: the pure gold for the forks, the basins and the pitchers; the weight of gold for each gold bowl, and the weight of silver for each silver bowl,
en.R: He told him about the pure gold for the meat forks, the bowls for sprinkling blood and the jars for pouring offerings. He also told him how much gold to use for each gold dish and how much silver for each silver dish.

decisions.choice: forks, basins, pitchers: tools for the sacrifices and offerings
decisions.reason: The forks were for handling the meat of the sacrifices (Exodus 27:3; 1 Samuel 2:13-14). The basins caught and sprinkled the blood (Exodus 27:3; Numbers 7:13). The pitchers held the wine poured out as drink offerings (Exodus 25:29; Numbers 4:7).

decisions.choice: bowls: a kind of covered bowl or dish
decisions.reason: This word is rare; it comes again only in the lists of temple vessels in Ezra 1:10 and 8:27. It seems to name a small bowl with a lid.

decisions.choice: pure gold
decisions.reason: The word means clean or pure. With gold it means gold without mixture, as in the tabernacle (Exodus 25:11, 17).

decisions.choice: meat forks; bowls for sprinkling blood; jars for pouring offerings
decisions.reason: Readable says what each vessel was used for (m1).

source.text: וּלְמִזְבַּ֧ח הַקְּטֹ֛רֶת זָהָ֥ב מְזֻקָּ֖ק בַּמִּשְׁקָ֑ל וּלְתַבְנִ֣ית הַמֶּרְכָּבָ֗ה הַכְּרֻבִ֤ים זָהָב֙ לְפֹ֣רְשִׂ֔ים וְסֹכְכִ֖ים עַל־אֲר֥וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and for [the] altar of the incense, gold refined by weight; and for [the] pattern of the chariot, the cherubim, gold, for spreading and covering over [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh.

en.L: and for the altar of incense, refined gold by weight; and for the pattern of the chariot, the cherubim, [of] gold, spreading [their wings] and covering the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: and the weight of refined gold for the altar of incense; and the plan for the chariot, the gold cherubim that spread their wings and cover the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: He told him how much refined gold to use for the altar where incense was burned. And he gave him the plan for God's chariot, the gold cherubim. These winged creatures would spread their wings over the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the chariot, the cherubim: the cherubim are God's chariot
decisions.reason: The two words stand side by side: "the chariot, the cherubim". Most likely the cherubim over the ark are themselves called a chariot, the throne-carriage on which the LORD rides as King: he "rode on a cherub and flew" (Psalm 18:11), and in Ezekiel 1 and 10 the cherubim with wheels carry his throne. It could instead mean "the chariot of the cherubim". This is the only place in the Old Testament where the cherubim of the ark are called a chariot.

decisions.choice: the cherubim spreading their wings over the ark
decisions.reason: Cherubim are winged heavenly creatures who guard God's presence (Genesis 3:24). Two gold cherubim were part of the mercy seat in the tabernacle (Exodus 25:18-20). In the temple Solomon made two large cherubim of olive wood covered in gold, whose wings stretched over the ark (1 Kings 6:23-28; 8:6-7; 2 Chronicles 3:10-13).

decisions.choice: spreading and covering: wings implied
decisions.reason: The verbs have no object; "wings" is understood, as in Exodus 25:20 and 1 Kings 8:7, where the cherubim spread their wings over the ark.

decisions.choice: the altar of incense: the gold altar in front of the inner room
decisions.reason: Incense was burned on it morning and evening (Exodus 30:1-10). It stood in the main hall before the inner room (1 Kings 6:20-22; 7:48).

decisions.choice: [their wings]; God's chariot
decisions.reason: Literal adds "their wings" in brackets and Balanced and Readable without (m3). Readable says the chariot is God's, the sense taken in m1, and explains that cherubim are winged creatures.

source.text: הַכֹּ֥ל בִּכְתָ֛ב מִיַּ֥ד יְהוָ֖ה עָלַ֣י הִשְׂכִּ֑יל כֹּ֖ל מַלְאֲכ֥וֹת הַתַּבְנִֽית׃פ

records.literal_gloss: The all in writing from [the] hand of Yahweh on me, he made understand, all [the] works of the pattern.

en.L: "All [this was] in writing from the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on me; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made [me] understand all the works of the pattern."
en.B: "All this," David said, "is in writing from the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} upon me. He made me understand all the details of the plan."
en.R: David said, "All this is written down. It came to me from the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He made me understand every detail of the plan."

decisions.choice: in writing from the hand of the LORD on me: the plan came from the LORD
alternatives: the LORD's hand was on me, and I wrote it down
the LORD gave it to me in writing by his own hand
decisions.reason: The words can be read in two ways. The hand of the LORD may have come on David, as it came on prophets when God gave them a message (2 Kings 3:15; Ezekiel 1:3), so that David wrote the plan down under God's guidance. Or the plan may have come to David as a writing from the LORD's own hand, as the tablets of the law were "written by the finger of God" (Exodus 31:18). Either way the design of the temple comes from God, as the design of the tabernacle did (Exodus 25:9, 40).

decisions.choice: on me: David speaks
decisions.reason: The verse begins with no words to say who is speaking, but "me" shows that these are David's words to Solomon, said as he hands over the plans.

decisions.choice: he made me understand all the works of the pattern: gave insight into every part of the design
decisions.reason: The verb means to give insight or understanding. "The works of the pattern" are the details of the design: everything listed in verses 11-18.

decisions.choice: David said
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "David said" so that the reader knows who is speaking (m2). Readable keeps both readings of m1 open by saying only that it came from the LORD's hand.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜יד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֗וֹ חֲזַ֤ק וֶאֱמַץ֙ וַעֲשֵׂ֔ה אַל־תִּירָ֖א וְאַל־תֵּחָ֑ת כִּי֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֤ים אֱלֹהַי֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ לֹ֤א יַרְפְּךָ֙ וְלֹ֣א יַֽעַזְבֶ֔ךָּ עַד־לִכְל֕וֹת כָּל־מְלֶ֖אכֶת עֲבוֹדַ֥ת בֵּית־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David to Solomon his son, Be strong and be bold and act; do not fear and do not be dismayed, for Yahweh God, my God, [is] with you; not he will let you drop, and not he will forsake you, until completing all [the] work of [the] service of [the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And David said to Solomon his son, "Be strong and bold, and act. Do not fear and do not be dismayed, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God, my God, [is] with you. He will not let you go, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not abandon you, until all the work for the service of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is finished.
en.B: David said to his son Solomon, "Be strong and courageous, and do the work. Do not be afraid or lose heart, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God, my God, is with you. He will not let go of you or abandon you until you have finished all the work for the service of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house.
en.R: Then David said to his son Solomon, "Be strong and brave, and do the work. Do not be afraid or lose heart. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God, my God, is with you. He will not let go of you or leave you on your own until all the work for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple is finished.

decisions.choice: the charge of Moses to Joshua
decisions.reason: Almost every phrase here comes from Moses' charge to Joshua and God's words to him: "Be strong and bold ... do not fear and do not be dismayed ... he will not let you go and he will not abandon you" (Deuteronomy 31:6-8; Joshua 1:5-9). David hands on his work to Solomon as Moses handed on his to Joshua. Joshua was to bring the people into the land; Solomon is to build the house where God will rest among them. David has said much the same to Solomon in 22:13.

decisions.choice: he will not let you go: he will not let you drop
decisions.reason: The verb means to let something sink or fall slack, and so to let go of someone or leave him without help, as in Joshua 1:5 and Deuteronomy 31:6, 8.

decisions.choice: the LORD God, my God, is with you: the ground of courage
decisions.reason: Solomon is to be strong not in his own strength but because David's God is with him until the work is done.

decisions.choice: be strong and bold / be strong and courageous / be strong and brave
decisions.reason: The same wording at each level as in Joshua, for the same Hebrew. "Do not fear and do not be dismayed" follows Deuteronomy 31:8, and "let you go ... abandon" follows Joshua 1:5.

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֗ה מַחְלְקוֹת֙ הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם לְכָל־עֲבוֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְעִמְּךָ֙ בְכָל־מְלָאכָ֜ה לְכָל־נָדִ֤יב בַּֽחָכְמָה֙ לְכָל־עֲבוֹדָ֔ה וְהַשָּׂרִ֥ים וְכָל־הָעָ֖ם לְכָל־דְּבָרֶֽיךָ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And see, [the] divisions of the priests and the Levites for all [the] service of [the] house of God; and with you in all [the] work [is] every willing [one] with skill for every service, and the officials and all the people for all your words.

en.L: And see, the divisions of the priests and the Levites [are here] for all the service of the house of God; and with you in all the work [will be] every willing [one] with skill for any service, and the princes and all the people [are ready] for all your words."
en.B: Look, here are the divisions of the priests and the Levites for every kind of service in the house of God. Every willing person with skill for any kind of service will be with you in all the work, and the officials and all the people will do whatever you command."
en.R: The groups of priests and Levites are ready to do all the work of God's temple. Everyone who is willing and skilled in any kind of work will help you. The leaders and all the people will do whatever you tell them."

decisions.choice: the divisions of the priests and the Levites
decisions.reason: As in verse 13: the groups David set in order in chapters 23-26 are ready to begin the work of the temple.

decisions.choice: every willing one with skill: those who freely offer themselves and have the craft for the work
decisions.reason: The first word describes someone whose heart moves him to give or serve freely, as the people gave for the tabernacle (Exodus 35:5, 22) and will give for the temple (29:5-9). The second word, often "wisdom", is also skill in a craft, as with the makers of the tabernacle (Exodus 31:3, 6; 35:31).

decisions.choice: for all your words: ready to do whatever you command
decisions.reason: To be "for" someone's words is to be at his command, ready to obey.

decisions.choice: princes / officials / leaders
decisions.reason: As in verse 1. Here, beside "all the people", the word means the leaders of the nation, not army commanders.

decisions.choice: Look / (not given)
decisions.reason: The opening word calls attention to what follows. Balanced says "Look"; Readable leaves it out, since the plain statement does the same work.
